issues.legal_issue: Limitation for executing a partition decree does not begin until a final decree that determines the parties’ rights is drawn up and engrossed on stamped paper, so an application to complete that decree is not barred merely because time has passed since the direction to prepare it.
material_facts: The preliminary decree declared the parties’ shares but left the partition of the properties to be worked out through further proceedings.
One party supplied stamped paper and obtained a decree concerning only that party’s share; the rights concerning the remaining shares and properties were not fully determined.
No commissioner was appointed and no complete final decree dividing the properties was drawn up and engrossed on stamped paper.
The other parties later applied to supply stamped paper and obtain a final decree, and the application was opposed as time-barred.
issues.conclusion: The application was not barred by limitation. The appeals were allowed, the High Court’s orders were set aside, and the trial court was directed to pass and engross the final decree before proceeding with execution.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 2(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, a decree is the formal expression of an adjudication that conclusively determines rights; Order 20 Rules 7 and 18(2) govern the drawing of decrees and partition decrees. A preliminary partition decree declares shares but does not itself complete the partition where further inquiry is required. Under Article 182 of the First Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1908, limitation for execution applies to an executable decree; a partition decree becomes executable only when the final decree determining the rights is drawn up and engrossed on the required stamped paper. Sections 2(a) and 34 and Article 46 of Schedule I of the Bombay Stamp Act, 1958, as amended, support the requirement that the decree be stamped. The Court relied on Rameshwar Singh v. Homeswar Singh for the principle that limitation applies only where the decree is capable of enforcement, distinguished Yeshwant v. Walchand, rejected Maksudan Prasad v. Smt. Lakshmi Devi as incorrectly decided, and approved Smt. Kotipalli Mahalakshmamma v. K. Ganeswara Rao.

rule.if: partition_proceeding and preliminary_decree_declared_shares and further_partition_work_required and not complete_final_decree_drawn_and_stamped

predicates.partition_proceeding: The proceeding is a suit to partition property or obtain separate possession of a share.
predicates.preliminary_decree_declared_shares: The court declared the parties’ shares but did not itself complete the partition.
predicates.further_partition_work_required: Further inquiry or other partition work remained necessary to determine and divide the parties’ property rights.
predicates.complete_final_decree_drawn_and_stamped: A final decree determining the rights at issue has been drawn up and engrossed on stamped paper.

issues.definition: When a partition proceeding requires further work after a preliminary decree and no complete stamped final decree has been drawn up, an application to obtain that final decree is not barred by limitation merely because time has passed since the direction to prepare it.
